correctness.rationale: Gaussian Laguerre expansion gives an exact covariance (including the diagonal), and Parseval isolates a rigorously quantified first-chaos term. Abel/summation-by-parts Fourier bounds and weighted Riemann sums prove the alpha<1/2 constant, fixed-parameter first-chaos dominance through alpha=1, positive limiting variance for alpha>1, and both compact-uniform 1/log n critical windows. The proof establishes all quantifiers, endpoints and integral convergence. FFT/Parseval and independent root-based Monte Carlo checks corroborate but are not used in place of analytic estimates.

value.rationale: The variance exhibits two distinct critical exponents: alpha=1/2 separates a regime where all logarithmic Gaussian chaoses contribute at leading order from first-chaos dominance; alpha=1 separates vanishing variance from a positive limiting variance. Two explicit compact-uniform logarithmic crossover functions quantify those changes. This is a natural spectral/moment invariant of Gaussian Taylor truncations and supplies substantive structural information not reducible to the unweighted alpha=0 constant.
